title: Simplicity of zeta zeros
open: Prove that all nontrivial zeros of \(\zeta(s)\) have multiplicity one. This is separate from their lying on the critical line.
status: Studied since early zeta theory. Positive proportions are provably simple; neither simplicity of every zero nor an unconditional density-one theorem is known.
why: Multiple zeros affect explicit formulas and distinguish conjectural models of prime fluctuations.
key_works: Hugh Montgomery (1973), *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, [DOI:10.1090/pspum/024/9944](https://doi.org/10.1090/pspum/024/9944); Kyle Pratt, Nicolas Robles, Alexandru Zaharescu and Dirk Zeindler (2020), *More than five-twelfths of the zeros of ζ are on the critical line*, [arXiv:1802.10521](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.10521).

title: Montgomery pair correlation
open: Show that distinct, locally rescaled zeta zeros have pair-correlation density
status: Conjectured in 1973. Montgomery proved a restricted Fourier-support range assuming RH; unrestricted correlations remain open.
why: Would connect fine prime fluctuations to local eigenvalue statistics of random Hermitian matrices.
key_works: Hugh Montgomery (1973), *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/pspum/024/9944); [Montgomery’s research page](https://public.websites.umich.edu/~hlm/pc.html).

title: Lindelöf hypothesis
open: Prove \(\zeta(1/2+it)=O_\varepsilon((1+|t|)^\varepsilon)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
status: Proposed in 1908. Subconvexity gives positive power bounds; Bourgain’s published exponent \(13/84+\varepsilon\) is a major benchmark. RH implies Lindelöf, but the converse is unknown.
why: Would provide nearly optimal cancellation estimates underlying divisor problems, short sums, and moment calculations.
key_works: Jean Bourgain (2017), *Decoupling, exponential sums and the Riemann zeta function*, [arXiv:1408.5794](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.5794), [DOI:10.1090/jams/860](https://doi.org/10.1090/jams/860).

title: Binary Goldbach conjecture
open: Prove that every even integer greater than two is the sum of two primes.
status: Originates in Goldbach’s 1742 correspondence with Euler. Chen’s theorem permits one summand to have at most two prime factors; published exhaustive verification reaches \(4\times10^{18}\).
why: Would settle a basic universal additive representation problem for primes and breach a longstanding sieve obstruction.
key_works: Tomás Oliveira e Silva, Siegfried Herzog and Silvio Pardi (2014), *Empirical verification of the even Goldbach conjecture and computation of prime gaps up to \(4\cdot10^{18}\)*, [author record](https://sweet.ua.pt/tos/bib/4.12.html), [DOI:10.1090/S0025-5718-2013-02787-1](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-2013-02787-1).
aliases: Strong Goldbach conjecture; even Goldbach conjecture.

title: Twin prime conjecture
open: Prove that infinitely many primes \(p\) have \(p+2\) prime.
status: Classical, explicitly associated with de Polignac’s 1849 conjectures. Bounded-gap methods establish infinitely many consecutive-prime gaps at most 246; they do not force gap two.
why: Would establish a fixed prime-pair pattern beyond current parity-limited sieve methods.
key_works: D. H. J. Polymath (2014), *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes*, [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897), [DOI:10.1186/s40687-014-0012-7](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40687-014-0012-7).

title: Infinitely many primes of the form \(n^2+1\)
open: Prove that \(n^2+1\) is prime for infinitely many positive integers \(n\).
status: One of Landau’s four problems highlighted in 1912. Iwaniec proved in 1978 that infinitely many values have at most two prime factors, counted with multiplicity.
why: A fundamental test of prime-producing irreducible polynomials in one variable.
key_works: Henryk Iwaniec (1978), *Almost-primes represented by quadratic polynomials*, [DOI:10.1007/BF01578070](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01578070).

title: Legendre’s conjecture
open: Prove that every interval \(n^2<p<(n+1)^2\), for integer \(n\ge1\), contains a prime.
status: Usually dated to 1798. The classical Baker–Harman–Pintz theorem finds primes in sufficiently large intervals of length \(x^{0.525}\), which does not reach the required square-root scale.
why: Isolates the difficulty of obtaining uniform prime existence in short intervals.
key_works: Roger Baker, Glyn Harman and János Pintz (2001), *The Difference Between Consecutive Primes, II*, [DOI:10.1112/plms/83.3.532](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/83.3.532).

title: Cramér’s prime-gap upper bound
open: Prove or disprove \(p_{n+1}-p_n=O((\log p_n)^2)\). This asks for a constant-factor bound, without asserting Cramér’s disputed exact limiting constant.
status: Proposed in 1936. Unconditional uniform bounds remain polynomial in \(p_n\); refined random-prime models change predicted constants without proving the logarithmic-square bound.
why: Would determine the order of the largest local deserts among primes.
key_works: Andrew Granville (1995), *Harald Cramér and the distribution of prime numbers*, [DOI:10.1080/03461238.1995.10413946](https://doi.org/10.1080/03461238.1995.10413946); Baker, Harman and Pintz (2001), *The Difference Between Consecutive Primes, II*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/83.3.532).

title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
open: Prove that primes have level of distribution one: for each fixed \(\theta<1\), the summed maximal discrepancy over moduli \(q\le x^\theta\) is \(O_A(x/(\log x)^A)\) for every \(A>0\).
status: Formulated in 1968. Bombieri–Vinogradov supplies level \(1/2\); results beyond that level restrict moduli, residue classes, or averaging.
why: Would strengthen prime-pattern sieves and uniformity estimates across arithmetic progressions.
key_works: P. D. T. A. Elliott and Heini Halberstam (1968), *A conjecture in prime number theory* (bibliographic details verify); D. H. J. Polymath (2014), *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes*, [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897).

title: Chowla’s Liouville correlation conjecture
open: For every fixed set of distinct nonnegative integers \(h_1,\ldots,h_k\), prove
status: From Chowla’s 1965 program. Logarithmically averaged two-point and odd-order versions are established; the ordinary two-point average remains open, including shifts zero and one.
why: Gives a precise meaning to randomness in the parity of prime factorization.
key_works: Terence Tao (2016), *The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations*, [arXiv:1509.05422](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422); Tao and Joni Teräväinen (2017), *Odd order cases of the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture*, [arXiv:1710.02112](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02112).

title: Artin’s primitive root conjecture
open: For each integer \(a\ne-1\) that is not a perfect square, prove that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, with the predicted positive density and correction factors.
status: Proposed in 1927. Hooley established the prediction under suitable GRH assumptions in 1967; an unconditional proof remains unknown even for \(a=2\).
why: Explains when one integer generates multiplicative groups of prime fields.
key_works: Pieter Moree (2012), *Artin’s Primitive Root Conjecture—A Survey*, [DOI:10.1515/integers-2012-0043](https://doi.org/10.1515/integers-2012-0043).

title: Existence of odd perfect numbers
open: Determine whether any odd positive integer equals the sum of its proper positive divisors.
status: Has ancient roots. Ochem’s maintained computation reports that a hypothetical example exceeds \(10^{2200}\) and has at least 115 prime factors counted with multiplicity; the peer-reviewed 2012 benchmark was \(10^{1500}\).
why: Would settle whether the classical classification of even perfect numbers exhausts all possibilities.
key_works: Pascal Ochem and Michaël Rao (2012), *Odd perfect numbers are greater than \(10^{1500}\)*, [DOI:10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02563-4](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02563-4); Ochem, [maintained project](https://www.lirmm.fr/~ochem/opn/).

title: Lehmer’s totient problem
open: Determine whether a composite integer \(n\) can satisfy \(\varphi(n)\mid n-1\).
status: Asked in 1932. Any composite example must be odd, square-free, and satisfy severe size and prime-factor restrictions; these do not eliminate every possibility.
why: Would characterize primes by a simple divisibility condition if the conjectured impossibility holds.
key_works: D. H. Lehmer (1932), *On Euler’s totient function* (bibliographic details verify); S. D. Cohen and P. Hagis Jr. (1980), *On the number of prime factors of n if φ(n) divides n−1* (identifier verify); [Formal Conjectures source issue](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/issues/90).

title: Carmichael’s totient multiplicity conjecture
open: Prove that whenever \(\varphi(n)=m\), another positive integer \(n'\ne n\) satisfies \(\varphi(n')=m\).
status: Dates to 1907. Ford’s work gives enormous necessary lower bounds for a counterexample and settles other multiplicity questions, without excluding multiplicity one.
why: Would reveal universal redundancy in the inverse Euler-totient problem.
key_works: Kevin Ford (1998), *The distribution of totients*, [announcement](https://www.ford126.web.illinois.edu/wwwpapers/totients-era.pdf); revised treatment, [arXiv:1104.3264](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264).

title: Irrationality of Euler’s constant
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
status: Euler introduced the constant in the eighteenth century. Explicit approximants and equivalent criteria exist; none decides irrationality.
why: Would extend irrationality methods beyond families accessible to current logarithmic and hypergeometric techniques.
key_works: Jeffrey C. Lagarias (2013), *Euler’s constant: Euler’s work and modern developments*, [arXiv:1303.1856](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.1856), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01423-X).

title: Irrationality of \(\zeta(7)\)
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Prove that \(\zeta(7)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-7}\) is irrational.
status: Part of the longstanding odd-zeta problem. Infinitely many odd zeta values are irrational, but this does not identify each value. The September 2026 result for \(\zeta(5)\) does not automatically extend to seven.
why: Would advance explicit irrationality beyond the presently controlled special values.
key_works: Tanguy Rivoal (2000), *La fonction zêta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0764-4442(00)01624-4); Frank Calegari (2026), *zeta(5) is irrational*, [exposition](https://galoisrepresentations.org/2026/09/24/zeta5-is-irrational/).

title: Algebraic independence of \(e\) and \(\pi\)
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Prove that no nonzero polynomial \(P\in\mathbb Q[X,Y]\) satisfies \(P(e,\pi)=0\).
status: Both constants individually have been known transcendental since the nineteenth century. Joint independence remains open; even irrationality of each of \(e+\pi\) and \(e\pi\) separately is unproved.
why: Would establish independence between the two most familiar transcendental constants.

title: Littlewood’s conjecture
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Prove \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\|n\alpha\|\|n\beta\|=0\) for every pair of real numbers \(\alpha,\beta\), where \(\|x\|\) is distance to the nearest integer.
status: Proposed around 1930. Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss proved that the exceptional set has Hausdorff dimension zero; eliminating every exceptional pair remains open.
why: Would resolve a fundamental simultaneous multiplicative approximation problem.
key_works: Manfred Einsiedler, Anatole Katok and Elon Lindenstrauss (2006), *Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood’s conjecture*, [manuscript](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~einsiedl/EKLslnr.pdf).

title: Zaremba’s conjecture
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Find an absolute \(A\) such that every positive denominator \(q\) occurs in a reduced fraction \(a/q\) whose finite continued-fraction partial quotients are at most \(A\). The classical proposed value is \(A=5\).
status: Formulated in 1971. Bourgain–Kontorovich established a density-one result with an absolute bound; every denominator remains beyond current results.
why: Would provide uniformly controlled rational approximations at arbitrary prescribed denominators.
key_works: Jean Bourgain and Alex Kontorovich (2014), *On Zaremba’s conjecture*, [arXiv:1107.3776](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.3776), [Annals article](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2014/180-1/p03).

title: Unbounded partial quotients of the cube root of two
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Prove or disprove that the ordinary continued-fraction partial quotients of \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) are unbounded.
status: A classical instance of a nineteenth-century problem. Roth’s theorem restricts exceptionally accurate approximation but does not decide boundedness of the partial quotients.
why: Would reveal qualitative continued-fraction behavior for an explicit algebraic number of degree greater than two.
key_works: Yann Bugeaud (2012), *Distribution Modulo One and Diophantine Approximation*, [DOI:10.1017/CBO9781139017732](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139017732).

title: Markov-number uniqueness conjecture
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: If positive integers \(x\le y\le z\) satisfy \(x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz\), does \(z\) uniquely determine \(x,y\)?
status: Formulated by Frobenius in 1913. Numerous restricted cases, including important prime-power cases, are known; the full Markov tree remains unresolved.
why: Would determine whether the largest coordinate uniquely encodes a classical Diophantine configuration.
key_works: Martin Aigner (2013), *Markov’s Theorem and 100 Years of the Uniqueness Conjecture*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-319-00888-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-00888-2).
aliases: Frobenius uniqueness conjecture; Markoff uniqueness conjecture.

title: abc conjecture
open: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), prove that coprime positive integers \(a+b=c\) satisfy
status: Formulated by Masser and Oesterlé in 1985. Mochizuki’s claimed proof was published in 2021, but objections from Scholze–Stix remain unresolved in the wider community. This records a proof controversy rather than an uncontested theorem.
why: Would impose sweeping restrictions on integer equations and the interaction between addition and prime factorization.
key_works: Peter Scholze and Jakob Stix (2018), *Why abc is still a conjecture*, [manuscript](https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/WhyABCisStillaConjecture.pdf); Shinichi Mochizuki (2021), *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-Volume Computations and Set-Theoretic Foundations*, [publication](https://ems.press/journals/prims/articles/201528).

title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
open: For every elliptic curve over a number field, identify its Mordell–Weil rank with the order of vanishing of its \(L\)-function at \(s=1\), and prove the predicted leading-coefficient formula.
status: Developed in the 1960s. Over \(\mathbb Q\), analytic ranks zero and one have major rank and finiteness theorems; arbitrary ranks and the full leading-term formula remain open.
why: Would connect rational solutions of cubic equations to analytic information in their \(L\)-functions.
key_works: Andrew Wiles (2006), *The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture*, in *The Millennium Prize Problems*; [Clay statement and references](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture/).
prize: US$1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize, subject to the institute’s rules.

solved.paper: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for elliptic curves over Q

title: Finiteness of Tate–Shafarevich groups
open: Prove that \(\operatorname{Sha}(A/K)\) is finite for every abelian variety over a number field.
status: Emerged in the 1950s–1960s. Euler-system methods establish important elliptic-curve cases, including analytic rank at most one over \(\mathbb Q\); unrestricted rank remains open.
why: Would control failures of the local-to-global principle for principal homogeneous spaces.
key_works: M. L. Brown (2025), *Shafarevich-Tate Groups*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-71893-9](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-71893-9); Bjorn Poonen (2025), *The origins of the Tate conjecture*, [slides](https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/slides/tate2025.pdf).

title: Uniform bound for rational points on curves
open: For each number field \(K\) and genus \(g\ge2\), prove that a constant \(B(K,g)\) bounds \(\#C(K)\) for every smooth projective genus-\(g\) curve over \(K\).
status: A central uniformity question since the 1980s–1990s. Faltings proves curve-by-curve finiteness; Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger give bounds incorporating the Mordell–Weil rank.
why: Would turn individual finiteness into a uniform structural constraint.
key_works: Vesselin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao and Philipp Habegger (2021), *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*, [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276); Patricia Pacelli (1997), *Uniform boundedness for rational points*, [arXiv:alg-geom/9601004](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9601004).

title: Effective Mordell conjecture
open: Give an unconditional algorithm that takes equations for a smooth projective curve \(C/K\) of genus at least two, outputs all its \(K\)-rational points, and certifies completeness.
status: Faltings proved finiteness in 1983 without a general effective bound. Chabauty, descent, and other methods cover extensive families; García-Fritz–Pasten’s 2025 work adds effective cases.
why: Would turn an existence theorem into a universally terminating rational-point computation.
key_works: Natalia García-Fritz and Hector Pasten (2025), *Effective Mordell for curves with enough automorphisms*, [arXiv:2503.10443](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10443).

title: Vojta’s height inequality
open: For smooth projective \(X/K\), a normal-crossings divisor \(D\), ample divisor \(A\), finite set of places \(S\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), prove
status: Formulated in the 1980s. Roth’s theorem and several subspace-theorem results are special cases; the general inequality remains open.
why: Would unify major Diophantine approximation and rational-point conjectures.
key_works: Paul Vojta (1987), *Diophantine Approximations and Value Distribution Theory*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0072989); Vojta (2010), *Diophantine Approximation and Nevanlinna Theory*, [manuscript](https://math.berkeley.edu/~vojta/cime/cime.pdf).

title: Potential density on K3 surfaces
open: Prove that every K3 surface over a number field acquires a Zariski-dense set of rational points over some finite field extension.
status: Longstanding. Density is known for substantial classes admitting elliptic fibrations or sufficiently many automorphisms.
why: Tests arithmetic predictions for varieties with trivial canonical class.
key_works: Fedor Bogomolov and Yuri Tschinkel (2000), *Density of rational points on elliptic K3 surfaces*, [arXiv:math/9902092](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9902092); Brendan Hassett, *Potential density of rational points*, [lecture abstract](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~thaddeus/seattle/abstracts/hassett2.html).

title: Modularity of elliptic curves over number fields
open: Attach a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_K)\), with matching local \(L\)-factors, to every elliptic curve over an arbitrary number field \(K\).
status: The framework dates to the 1950s–1970s. All elliptic curves over \(\mathbb Q\) are modular, with major extensions over totally real fields; arbitrary number fields remain open.
why: Would extend analytic tools and automorphic structure throughout elliptic-curve arithmetic.
key_works: Jack A. Thorne (2023), *Elliptic curves and modularity*, [DOI:10.4171/8ECM/12](https://doi.org/10.4171/8ECM/12), [publisher chapter](https://ems.press/books/standalone/262/5175).

title: Fontaine–Mazur conjecture
open: Show that every irreducible \(p\)-adic Galois representation of a number field, unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham above \(p\), comes up to Tate twist from étale cohomology of an algebraic variety.
status: Formulated in 1995. Modularity-lifting results settle many two-dimensional cases under hypotheses; arbitrary dimensions remain open.
why: Would characterize arithmetic representations originating in geometry.
key_works: Jean-Marc Fontaine and Barry Mazur (1995), *Geometric Galois representations* (identifier verify); Ramla Abdellatif, Supriya Pisolkar, Marine Rougnant and Lara Thomas (2022), *From Fontaine-Mazur conjecture to analytic pro-p groups—a survey*, [arXiv:2205.03558](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03558).

title: Inverse Galois problem over \(\mathbb Q\)
open: Prove that every finite group occurs as \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)\) for a finite Galois extension \(L\), or exhibit a group that cannot.
status: A nineteenth-century question. All finite solvable groups and many nonabelian simple groups are realizable; a universal construction is unknown.
why: Would identify the full range of symmetries of polynomial equations over the rationals.
key_works: Gunter Malle and B. Heinrich Matzat (1999), *Inverse Galois Theory*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8); Tim Dokchitser, [research resource](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matyd/InvGal/).

title: Regular inverse Galois problem
open: For every finite group \(G\), construct a Galois extension \(L/\mathbb Q(t)\) with group \(G\) and \(L\cap\overline{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\).
status: Developed in twentieth-century geometric Galois theory. Rigidity and covers realize many groups; no universal construction is known.
why: Hilbert irreducibility would specialize such realizations to solve the ordinary inverse Galois problem.
key_works: Gunter Malle and B. Heinrich Matzat (1999), *Inverse Galois Theory*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8).

title: Hilbert’s twelfth problem for arbitrary number fields
open: For arbitrary \(K\), exhibit explicit analytic functions and special arguments whose values generate every finite abelian extension of \(K\), with proved algebraicity and reciprocity laws.
status: Posed in 1900. Cyclotomic and complex-multiplication theories solve classical cases; Dasgupta–Kakde construct maximal abelian extensions of totally real fields using \(p\)-adic integration. Arbitrary fields remain open.
why: Would make class field theory explicit through analytic special values.
key_works: Samit Dasgupta and Mahesh Kakde (2024), *Brumer–Stark Units and Explicit Class Field Theory*, [arXiv:2103.02516](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.02516); ICMS (2024), [*Recent Progress on Hilbert’s 12th Problem*](https://icms.ac.uk/archive/workshop/recent-progress-on-hilberts-12th-problem/).
aliases: Explicit class field theory; generalized Kronecker Jugendtraum.

title: Schinzel’s hypothesis H
open: For finitely many irreducible integer polynomials with positive leading coefficients whose product has no fixed prime divisor, prove that all their values are simultaneously prime infinitely often.
status: Formulated by Schinzel–Sierpiński in 1958. Limited linear configurations are accessible; even one quadratic such as \(n^2+1\) is open.
why: Would unify a large family of prime-producing polynomial conjectures.
key_works: Andrzej Schinzel and Wacław Sierpiński (1958), *Sur certaines hypothèses concernant les nombres premiers*, [DOI:10.4064/aa-4-3-185-208](https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-4-3-185-208).

title: Hodge conjecture
open: Prove that every rational cohomology class of type \((p,p)\) on a smooth complex projective variety is a rational linear combination of classes of codimension-\(p\) algebraic subvarieties.
status: Originates in Hodge’s work of the 1930s–1950s. Divisors and varieties of dimension at most three are covered; higher-codimension cases remain open.
why: Would identify which topological cohomology classes arise from algebraic geometry.
key_works: Pierre Deligne (2006), *The Hodge Conjecture*, in *The Millennium Prize Problems*; [Clay statement](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/hodge-conjecture/); Salvatore Floccari and Lie Fu (2025), *The Hodge conjecture for Weil fourfolds with discriminant 1 via singular OG6-varieties*, [arXiv:2504.13607](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13607).
prize: US$1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize, subject to the institute’s rules.

solved.paper: The Hodge standard conjecture for self-products of K3 surfaces

title: Generalized Hodge conjecture
open: For a rational sub-Hodge structure \(V\subset H^k(X,\mathbb Q)\) whose Hodge types have both indices at least \(p\), find an algebraic subset \(Z\subset X\) of codimension at least \(p\) such that \(V\) restricts to zero on \(X\setminus Z\).
status: Grothendieck formulated the corrected conjecture in 1969 after identifying a defect in Hodge’s original generalization. Special varieties and degrees are known.
why: Would connect Hodge-theoretic restrictions to geometric support of cohomology.
key_works: Alexander Grothendieck (1969), *Hodge’s general conjecture is false for trivial reasons*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(69)90016-0).

title: Hodge standard conjecture in positive characteristic
open: Prove positive definiteness of the signed intersection form
status: Proposed in the 1960s. Hodge theory handles characteristic zero; surfaces and abelian fourfolds are known in positive characteristic.
why: Would supply a missing positivity principle in the theory of algebraic cycles.
key_works: Giuseppe Ancona (2021), *Standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds*, [arXiv:1806.03216](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03216), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-020-00990-7).
aliases: Standard conjecture I; standard conjecture of Hodge type.

title: Bloch–Beilinson filtration
open: Construct the conjectural finite descending filtration on rational Chow groups, compatible with products and correspondences, with first step the homologically trivial cycles and graded pieces governed by cohomological motives.
status: Developed in the 1980s. Murre’s 1993 formulation uses Chow–Künneth projectors; curves, surfaces, and special motives admit substantial parts of the structure.
why: Would organize algebraic cycles by their successive levels of cohomological invisibility.
key_works: Jacob P. Murre (1993), *On a conjectural filtration on the Chow groups of an algebraic variety. I. The general conjectures and some examples*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0019-3577(93)90038-Z).

title: Bloch’s zero-cycle conjecture for surfaces with \(p_g=0\)
open: For every smooth projective complex surface \(S\) with geometric genus zero, prove that the Albanese map \(CH_0(S)^0\to\operatorname{Alb}(S)(\mathbb C)\) is an isomorphism.
status: Formulated in the 1970s. Known outside general type and for numerous special general-type families.
why: Would show that zero-cycles on these surfaces carry no hidden information beyond the Albanese variety.
key_works: Kalyan Banerjee (2025), *Bloch’s conjecture on certain surfaces of general type with \(p_g=0\) and with an involution: The Enriques case*, [publication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0019357725000321); Vladimir Guletskii and Claudio Pedrini (2003), *Finite dimensional motives and the Conjectures of Beilinson and Murre*, [arXiv:math/0303170](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303170).

title: Kimura–O’Sullivan finite-dimensionality
open: Prove that every smooth projective variety has a rational Chow motive \(M_+\oplus M_-\), with some exterior power of \(M_+\) and some symmetric power of \(M_-\) equal to zero.
status: Proposed around 2000. Known for motives of curves, abelian varieties, and varieties generated from them by appropriate motivic operations.
why: Would impose strong finiteness and nilpotence properties on algebraic correspondences.
key_works: Shun-ichi Kimura (2005), *Chow groups are finite dimensional, in some sense*, [DOI:10.1007/s00208-004-0577-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00208-004-0577-3); Guletskii and Pedrini (2003), [arXiv:math/0303170](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303170).

title: Resolution of singularities in positive characteristic
open: For every integral variety over a perfect field of positive characteristic, construct a proper birational morphism from a smooth variety that is an isomorphism over the original smooth locus.
status: Characteristic-zero resolution was proved in 1964. Low dimensions are known; the general problem from dimension four upward remains open. Alterations are generically finite and do not supply the required birational map.
why: Would extend many geometric constructions and arguments to positive characteristic.
key_works: Herwig Hauser (2010), *On the problem of resolution of singularities in positive characteristic (Or: A proof we are still waiting for)*, [DOI:10.1090/S0273-0979-09-01274-9](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-09-01274-9).

title: Strong factorization of birational maps
open: Given a birational map between smooth complete characteristic-zero varieties, find a smooth common model obtained from each solely by blowups along smooth centers.
status: Classical. Weak factorization, allowing interspersed blowups and blowdowns, was established around 2000; ordering all blowups before all blowdowns remains open.
why: Would provide a more rigid and constructive description of birational equivalence.
key_works: Dan Abramovich, Kalle Karu, Kenji Matsuki and Jarosław Włodarczyk (2002), *Torification and Factorization of Birational Maps*, [arXiv:math/9904135](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9904135), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00396-X).

title: Abundance conjecture
open: For a projective Kawamata log terminal pair \((X,\Delta)\) in characteristic zero, with rational boundary and nef \(K_X+\Delta\), prove that some positive integral multiple is base-point-free.
status: Central to the minimal model program since the 1980s. Established through dimension three and in many higher-dimensional special cases.
why: Would turn numerical positivity of the canonical divisor into a geometric fibration.
key_works: János Kollár and Shigefumi Mori (1998), *Birational Geometry of Algebraic Varieties*, [DOI:10.1017/CBO9780511662560](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511662560).

title: Nagata’s plane-curve conjecture
open: For nonsquare \(r\ge10\) and \(r\) very general points in \(\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}\), prove that a degree-\(d\) curve with multiplicities \(m_i\) at those points satisfies \(d\ge(\sum_i m_i)/\sqrt r\).
status: Proposed in 1959. Nagata proved the corresponding square-number case; nonsquare cases begin with ten points.
why: Would determine fundamental limits on interpolation by plane algebraic curves.
key_works: Carlos Galindo, Francisco Monserrat, Carlos-Jesús Moreno-Ávila and Julio José Moyano-Fernández (2025), *On the valuative Nagata conjecture*, [arXiv:2208.11041](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11041), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40687-025-00500-2).

title: Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz conjecture
open: Prove that every special linear system of plane curves with multiplicities at very general points is explained by fixed \((-1)\)-curves: removing the forced components leaves the expected dimension.
status: Originates with Segre in 1961 and later refinements. Many bounded-multiplicity and homogeneous cases are settled; arbitrary multiplicity lists remain open.
why: Would classify failures of expected dimension in plane-curve interpolation.
key_works: Maria Chiara Brambilla and Elisa Postinghel (2025), *Towards Good Postulation of Fat Points, One Step at a Time*, [DOI:10.1007/s40574-025-00468-5](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40574-025-00468-5).

title: Hartshorne complete-intersection conjecture
open: Prove that every smooth complex projective \(X\subset\mathbb P^{n+c}\) of dimension \(n\ge2c+1\) is a complete intersection.
status: Proposed in 1974. Important classes, including varieties defined by quadrics, are known; the general small-codimension case remains open.
why: Would show that sufficiently low codimension forces an exceptionally simple equation structure.
key_works: Robin Hartshorne (1974), *Varieties of small codimension in projective space* (identifier verify); Kiwamu Watanabe (2025), *Quadratic Varieties of Small Codimension*, [arXiv:2405.04002](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04002), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.3842/SIGMA.2025.045).

title: Existence of Ulrich bundles
open: For every smooth projective variety with a fixed very ample \(\mathcal O_X(1)\), construct a nonzero vector bundle \(E\) with \(H^i(X,E(-j))=0\) for all \(0\le i\le\dim X\) and \(1\le j\le\dim X\).
status: Prominent since the early 2000s. Many curves, surfaces, homogeneous varieties, and double-cover cases are covered.
why: Would supply optimally behaved vector bundles and linear algebraic presentations on every polarized variety.
key_works: N. Mohan Kumar, Poornapushkala Narayanan and A. J. Parameswaran (2025), *Ulrich bundles on double covers of projective spaces*, [arXiv:2201.08703](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.08703).

title: Cancellation for affine three-space in characteristic zero
open: If an affine complex variety \(X\) satisfies \(X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^4\), must \(X\cong\mathbb A^3\)?
status: Zariski’s question dates to the mid-twentieth century. Dimensions one and two are known; Gupta’s positive-characteristic counterexamples leave this case open.
why: Would determine whether an affine-line factor can conceal nontrivial algebraic geometry.
key_works: Neena Gupta (2014), *On Zariski’s Cancellation Problem in positive characteristic*, [arXiv:1309.1368](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.1368); Parnashree Ghosh (2026), [IISc seminar on cancellation](https://math.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026/2026-04-22-parnashree-ghosh.html).

title: Huneke–Wiegand torsion conjecture
open: For a one-dimensional Gorenstein local domain \(R\), prove that every nonfree finitely generated torsion-free \(M\) has torsion in \(M\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\).
status: Proposed in 1994. Hypersurface cases and numerous special modules are understood; higher-codimension complete intersections remain open in general.
why: Would connect tensor-product behavior to the freeness and rigidity of modules.
key_works: Craig Huneke and Roger Wiegand (1994), *Tensor products of modules and the rigidity of Tor*, [record](https://geodesic.mathdoc.fr/item/MAN_1994__299_4_165218/); Rafael Holanda and Cleto B. Miranda-Neto (2025), *An Ext-Tor duality theorem, cohomological dimension, and applications*, [arXiv:2312.09725](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09725).

title: Eisenbud–Mazur symbolic-square conjecture
open: For a prime \(P\) in a regular local ring \((R,\mathfrak m)\) containing \(\mathbb Q\), prove \(P^{(2)}\subseteq\mathfrak mP\), where \(P^{(2)}=P^2R_P\cap R\).
status: Proposed in the 1990s. Low-codimension and linkage cases are known; positive-characteristic analogues can fail.
why: Would constrain infinitesimal deformations and the difference between symbolic and ordinary powers.
key_works: David Eisenbud and Barry Mazur (1997), *Evolutions, Symbolic Squares, and Fitting Ideals*, [arXiv:alg-geom/9511008](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9511008), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1997.488.189).

title: Lech’s multiplicity conjecture in mixed characteristic
open: For every flat local map of Noetherian local rings \(R\to S\), with \(R\) of mixed characteristic, prove \(e(R)\le e(S)\) for Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities.
status: Proposed in 1960. Low-dimensional and special cases are known. An October 6, 2026 preliminary exposition addresses equal characteristic; mixed characteristic remains a separate target.
why: Would show that flat extension cannot reduce this measure of local singularity complexity.
key_works: Linquan Ma (2017), *Lech’s conjecture in dimension three*, [arXiv:1609.00095](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00095); Srikanth B. Iyengar, Linquan Ma and Mark Walker (2026), *Lech’s conjecture in equal characteristic*, [preliminary exposition](https://mark-walker-22.github.io/Lech.html).

title: Ramanujan conjecture for Hecke–Maass forms
open: For every normalized Hecke–Maass cusp form on \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H\), prove \(|\lambda_f(p)|\le2\) for every prime \(p\), in unitary normalization.
status: The Maass-form extension of Ramanujan’s problem remains open. Kim–Sarnak’s exponent \(7/64\) gives \(|\lambda_f(p)|\le p^{7/64}+p^{-7/64}\).
why: Would give optimal local bounds for these automorphic representations.
key_works: Henry H. Kim and Peter Sarnak (2003), *Refined estimates towards the Ramanujan and Selberg conjectures*, Appendix 2 to Kim’s functoriality paper, [DOI:10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00410-1](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00410-1).

title: Mumford–Tate conjecture for abelian varieties
open: For every abelian variety over a number field, prove that the identity component of its \(\ell\)-adic algebraic monodromy group equals its Mumford–Tate group over \(\mathbb Q_\ell\).
status: Proposed in the 1960s. Known for elliptic curves, CM abelian varieties, and many additional classes; arbitrary dimension remains open.
why: Would identify the compatibility between Hodge-theoretic and Galois-theoretic symmetries.
key_works: Victoria Cantoral Farfán (2016), *A survey around the Hodge, Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures for abelian varieties*, [arXiv:1602.08354](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.08354); Richard Pink (1998), *l-adic algebraic monodromy groups, cocharacters, and the Mumford-Tate conjecture*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1998.018).

title: Broué’s abelian-defect-group conjecture
open: For a block of a finite group algebra in characteristic \(p\) with abelian defect group \(D\), prove that its bounded derived module category is equivalent to that of its Brauer-correspondent block in \(N_G(D)\).
status: Proposed in 1990. Cyclic-defect blocks and many group families are known; arbitrary abelian-defect blocks remain open.
why: Would relate global modular representation theory to local subgroup data.
key_works: Michel Broué (1990), *Isométries parfaites, types de blocs, catégories dérivées*, [original](https://numdam.org/item/AST_1990__181-182__61_0/); Jeremy Rickard, [problem statement](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~majcr/adgc/what.html).

title: Goldberg conjecture in negative scalar curvature
open: Must every compact Einstein almost-Kähler manifold be Kähler? The remaining issue is negative scalar curvature with a nonintegrable compatible almost-complex structure.
status: Proposed in 1969. Sekigawa proved the nonnegative-scalar-curvature case in 1987; noncompact examples do not settle the compact case.
why: Would establish a strong compatibility between Einstein geometry and symplectic structure.
key_works: Kouei Sekigawa (1987), *On some compact Einstein almost Kähler manifolds*; Vestislav Apostolov and Tedi Drăghici (2003), *The curvature and the integrability of almost-Kähler manifolds: a survey*, [arXiv:math/0302152](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0302152).

title: Chern’s discreteness conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces
open: For fixed \(n\), is the set of constant scalar curvatures realized by closed minimal hypersurfaces of \(S^{n+1}\) discrete?
status: Originates in Chern’s questions from the 1960s–1980s. Simons-type gap theorems exclude intervals but do not establish global discreteness.
why: Would impose a discrete structure on constant-curvature minimal hypersurfaces.
key_works: James Simons (1968), *Minimal varieties in Riemannian manifolds*; Jianquan Ge and Fagui Li (2021; revised 2025), *Integral-Einstein hypersurfaces in spheres*, [arXiv:2101.03753](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03753).

title: Infinitely many prime closed geodesics on higher-dimensional spheres
open: Does every smooth Riemannian metric on \(S^n\), \(n\ge3\), possess infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics?
status: A classical twentieth-century problem. The two-sphere case is settled; loop-space topology gives powerful sufficient conditions that do not cover arbitrary higher-dimensional sphere metrics.
why: Would establish unavoidable complexity in geodesic dynamics on spheres.
key_works: Detlef Gromoll and Wolfgang Meyer (1969), *Periodic geodesics on compact Riemannian manifolds*; Keith Burns and Vladimir Matveev (2013; updated 2019), *Open problems and questions about geodesics*, [arXiv:1308.5417](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.5417).

title: Smooth Hamiltonian Seifert problem in four dimensions
open: Is there a \(C^\infty\) Hamiltonian on \(\mathbb R^4\) with a compact regular energy hypersurface containing no periodic trajectory?
status: Smooth examples exist in higher dimensions. Ginzburg–Gürel constructed a \(C^2\) example in dimension four in 2003; the \(C^\infty\) case remains open.
why: Would determine whether smoothness forces periodic dynamics at this dimensional boundary.
key_works: Viktor Ginzburg and Başak Gürel (2003), *A C2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R4*, [arXiv:math/0110047](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0110047), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2003.158.953).

title: Smooth four-dimensional Schoenflies conjecture
open: Does every smooth embedding \(S^3\hookrightarrow S^4\) bound a standard smooth four-ball on each side?
status: The remaining smooth dimension is longstanding. Topological Schoenflies is known; recent work connects the smooth problem to pseudo-isotopies of \(S^1\times S^3\).
why: Would classify the smooth regions cut out by embedded three-spheres in \(S^4\).
key_works: Morton Brown (1960), *A proof of the generalized Schoenflies theorem*; David Gabai (2022), *3-Spheres in the 4-Sphere and Pseudo-Isotopies of S1×S3*, [arXiv:2212.02004](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02004).

title: Eleven-eighths conjecture

status: Attributed to Matsumoto in 1982. Furuta proved the ten-eighths inequality with an additive correction; later equivariant refinements improve particular congruence classes.
why: Would sharply constrain intersection forms of smooth spin four-manifolds.
key_works: Mikio Furuta (2001), *Monopole equation and the 11/8-conjecture*; Michael Hopkins, Jianfeng Lin, XiaoLin Danny Shi and Zhouli Xu (2022), *Intersection Forms of Spin 4-Manifolds and the Pin(2)-Equivariant Mahowald Invariant*, [arXiv:1812.04052](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04052).

title: Exotic smooth structure on the complex projective plane

status: Open since the emergence of exotic simply connected four-manifolds in the 1980s. Exotic structures exist on many blowups; the unblown-up projective plane remains unresolved.
why: Would locate the smallest possible complexity of exotic simply connected smooth four-manifolds.
key_works: Robion Kirby (1997), *Problems in low-dimensional topology*, [author collection](https://math.berkeley.edu/~kirby/); Robert Gompf and András Stipsicz (1999), *4-Manifolds and Kirby Calculus*.

title: Geometric simple connectivity of closed simply connected four-manifolds
open: Does every closed simply connected smooth four-manifold admit a handle decomposition without one-handles, without changing the manifold by stabilization?
status: A classical Kirby-list problem. Many examples admit such decompositions; boundary counterexamples do not answer the closed case.
why: Would make algebraic simple connectivity visible directly in handle structure.
key_works: Robion Kirby (1997), *Problems in low-dimensional topology*; Kouichi Yasui (2019), *Geometrically simply connected 4-manifolds and stable cohomotopy Seiberg-Witten invariants*, [arXiv:1807.11453](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11453).

title: Topological surgery in dimension four for arbitrary fundamental groups

status: Freedman’s theory and later work handle large classes, including subexponential-growth groups. Free fundamental groups remain central test cases.
why: Would extend the principal classification method for high-dimensional manifolds to unrestricted four-dimensional topology.
key_works: Michael Freedman and Frank Quinn (1990), *Topology of 4-Manifolds*; Freedman and Vyacheslav Krushkal (2016), *Engel relations in 4-manifold topology*, [arXiv:1412.5024](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5024).

title: Jones polynomial detection of the unknot
open: If the normalized Jones polynomial of a knot is \(1\), must the knot be the unknot?
status: Open since the invariant’s introduction in 1984–1985. Many families and finite tables are checked; Khovanov homology detects the unknot, but that stronger invariant does not settle this question.
why: Would determine whether the Jones polynomial detects the simplest knot type.
key_works: Vaughan Jones (1985), *A polynomial invariant for knots via von Neumann algebras*; Peter Kronheimer and Tomasz Mrowka (2011), *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, [arXiv:1005.4346](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4346).

title: Volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots

status: Kashaev proposed the volume-growth phenomenon in 1997; Murakami–Murakami connected it to colored Jones polynomials in 2001. Selected knots and families are known.

title: Ryser's conjecture
open: relating the maximum [[Matching in hypergraphs|matching]] size and minimum [[Vertex cover in hypergraphs|transversal]] size in [[hypergraph]]s

title: Woodall's conjecture
open: that the minimum number of edges in a [[dicut]] of a [[directed graph]] is equal to the maximum number of disjoint [[dijoin]]s

title: Tarski's exponential function problem
open: is the [[Theory (mathematical logic)|theory]] of the [[real number]]s with the [[exponential function]] [[Decidability (logic)#Decidability of a theory|decidable]]?

title: Büchi's problem
open: on sufficiently large sequences of square numbers with constant second difference

title: Carmichael's totient function conjecture
open: do all values of [[Euler's totient function]] have [[Multiplicity (mathematics)|multiplicity]] greater than 1?

title: Catalan–Dickson conjecture on aliquot sequences
open: no [[aliquot sequence]]s are infinite but non-repeating

title: Exponent pair conjecture
open: for all \varepsilon > 0, is the pair (\varepsilon, 1/2 + \varepsilon) an [[Van der Corput's method#Exponent pairs|exponent pair]]?

title: Grimm's conjecture
open: each element of a set of consecutive [[composite number]]s can be assigned a distinct [[prime number]] that divides it

title: Hall's conjecture
open: for any \varepsilon > 0, there is some constant c(\varepsilon) such that either y^2 = x^3 or |y^2 - x^3| > c(\varepsilon)x^{1/2 - \varepsilon}

title: Magic square of squares
open: is there a 3x3 magic square composed of distinct perfect squares?

title: Mahler's 3/2 problem
open: that no real number x has the property that the fractional parts of x(3/2)^n are less than 1/2 for all positive integers n

title: Scholz conjecture
open: the length of the shortest [[addition chain]] producing 2^n - 1 is at most n - 1 plus the length of the shortest addition chain producing n

title: Singmaster's conjecture
open: is there a finite upper bound on the multiplicities of the entries greater than 1 in [[Pascal's triangle]]?

title: Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases
open: if B is an [[additive basis]] of order 2, then the number of ways that positive integers n can be expressed as the sum of two numbers in B must tend to infinity as n tends to infinity

title: Lemoine's conjecture
open: all odd integers greater than 5 can be represented as the sum of an odd [[prime number]] and an even [[semiprime]]

title: Skolem problem
open: can an algorithm determine if a [[constant-recursive sequence]] contains a zero?

title: Hermite's problem
open: is it possible, for any natural number n, to assign a sequence of [[natural number]]s to each [[real number]] such that the sequence for x is eventually [[Periodic sequence|periodic]] if and only if x is [[Algebraic number|algebraic]] of degree n?

title: Kummer–Vandiver conjecture
open: primes p do not divide the [[Ideal class group#Properties|class number]] of the maximal real [[Field extension|subfield]] of the p-th [[cyclotomic field]]

title: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture
open: the normalized pair [[correlation function]] between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function is the same as the pair correlation function of [[Random matrix#Gaussian ensembles|random Hermitian matrices]]

title: Piltz divisor problem
open: on bounding \Delta_k(x) = D_k(x) - xP_k(\log(x))

title: Selberg's 1/4 conjecture
open: the [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors|eigenvalues]] of the [[Laplace operator]] on [[Maass wave form]]s of [[congruence subgroup]]s are at least 1/4

title: Selberg's orthogonality conjecture
open: generalization of [[Mertens' theorems#Second theorem|Mertens' theorem]] for functions in Selberg class

title: Erdős–Ulam problem
open: Is there a [[dense set]] of points in the plane all at rational distances from one another?

title: Zilber–Pink conjecture
open: that if X is a mixed [[Shimura variety]] or [[Abelian variety#Semiabelian variety|semiabelian variety]] defined over \mathbb{C}, and V \subseteq X is a subvariety, then V contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties

title: Littlewood conjecture
open: for any two real numbers \alpha, \beta, \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} n\,\Vert n\alpha\Vert\,\Vert n\beta\Vert = 0, where \Vert x\Vert is the distance from x to the nearest integer

title: Beal's conjecture
open: for all integral solutions to A^x + B^y = C^z where x, y, z > 2, all three numbers A, B, C must share some prime factor

title: Brocard's problem
open: are there any integer solutions to n! + 1 = m^{2} other than n = 4, 5, 7?

title: Congruent number problem
open: (a corollary to [[Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]], per [[Tunnell's theorem]]): determine precisely what rational numbers are [[congruent number]]s

title: Goormaghtigh conjecture
open: on solutions to (x^m - 1)/(x - 1) = (y^n - 1)/(y - 1) where x > y > 1 and m, n > 2

title: Pillai's conjecture
open: for any A, B, C, the equation Ax^m - By^n = C has finitely many solutions when m, n are not both 2

title: Agoh–Giuga conjecture
open: on the [[Bernoulli number]]s that p is prime if and only if pB_{p-1} \equiv -1 \pmod p

title: Agrawal's conjecture
open: that given [[Coprime integers|coprime positive integers]] n and r, if (X - 1)^n \equiv X^n - 1 \pmod{n, X^r - 1}, then either n is prime or n^{2} \equiv 1 \pmod{r}

title: Artin's conjecture on primitive roots
open: that if an integer is neither a perfect square nor -1, then it is a [[Primitive root modulo n|primitive root]] modulo infinitely many [[prime number]]s p

title: Brocard's conjecture
open: there are always at least 4 [[prime number]]s between consecutive squares of prime numbers, aside from 2^{2} and 3^{2}

title: Bunyakovsky conjecture
open: if an integer-coefficient polynomial f has a positive leading coefficient, is irreducible over the integers, and has no common factors over all f(x) where x is a positive integer, then f(x) is prime infinitely often

title: Dickson's conjecture
open: for a finite set of linear forms a_1 + b_1 n, \ldots, a_k + b_k n with each b_i \geq 1, there are infinitely many n for which all forms are [[prime number|prime]], unless there is some [[Modular arithmetic|congruence]] condition preventing it

title: Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture
open: no three consecutive numbers are all [[Powerful number|powerful]]

title: Feit–Thompson conjecture
open: for all distinct [[prime number]]s p and q, (p^q - 1)/(p - 1) does not divide (q^p - 1)/(q - 1)

title: New Mersenne conjecture
open: for any odd [[natural number]] p, if any two of the three conditions p = 2^k \pm 1 or p = 4^k \pm 3, 2^p - 1 is prime, and (2^{p} + 1)/3 is prime are true, then the third condition is also true

title: Polignac's conjecture
open: for all positive even numbers n, there are infinitely many [[prime gap]]s of size n

title: Selfridge's conjecture
open: is 78,557 the lowest [[Sierpiński number]]?

title: Siegel's conjecture
open: are there infinitely many regular primes, and if so is their [[natural density]] as a subset of all primes e^{-1/2}?

title: Reinhardt cardinal
open: s: Without assuming the [[axiom of choice]], can a [[Reinhardt cardinal|nontrivial elementary embedding]] V→V exist?

title: Berge conjecture
open: that the only [[Knot (mathematics)|knots]] in the [[3-sphere]] which admit [[lens space]] [[Dehn surgery|surgeries]] are [[Berge knot]]s

title: Bing–Borsuk conjecture
open: every n-dimensional [[Homogeneous space|homogeneous]] [[Retraction (topology)|absolute neighborhood retract]] is a [[topological manifold]]

title: Borel conjecture
open: [[Aspherical space|aspherical]] and [[closed manifold]]s are determined up to [[homeomorphism]] by their [[fundamental group]]s

title: Hilbert–Smith conjecture
open: if a [[Locally compact space|locally compact]] [[topological group]] has a [[Continuous function|continuous]], [[Group action#Remarkable properties of actions|faithful group action]] on a [[topological manifold]], then the group must be a [[Lie group]]

title: Whitehead conjecture
open: every [[Connectedness|connected]] [[CW complex#Inductive construction of CW complexes|subcomplex]] of a two-dimensional [[Aspherical space|aspherical]] [[CW complex]] is aspherical

title: Zeeman conjecture
open: given a finite [[Contractible space|contractible]] two-dimensional [[CW complex]] K, is the space K \times [0, 1] [[Collapse (topology)|collapsible]]?

title: Ringel's conjecture
open: that the [[complete graph]] K_{2n+1} can be decomposed into 2n+1 copies of any tree with n edges ([[Richard Montgomery (mathematician)|Richard Montgomery]], [[Benny Sudakov]], [[Alexey Pokrovskiy]], 2020)
